scope: Line-by-line review performed by session `6ddde224` (T-COVERAGE-FULL) on 2026-10-14. Every claim carries the exact source link used for it; anything that could not be confirmed stays blank. `read_at_utc` is when this session read the source.

items.claim: bo3.gg /api/v1/matches pages by `page[limit]` + `page[offset]`; a plain `page` parameter is ignored.
items.method: Three direct reads of the live feed: `page=2` and `page[number]=2` returned page 1 unchanged, while `page[offset]=20` advanced to the 21st record.
items.note: The first crawl (built with plain `page`) held 5,000 rows for only 10 distinct matches. That snapshot is deleted and re-crawled; the collector now refuses to reuse a corpus that fails a distinct-id/span check.

items.claim: The book price pair bo3.gg keeps for a finished match is a closing (pre-match) line usable as a benchmark.
items.method: Scored the committed corpus: the pair implied the eventual winner in 100% of 4,000 settled matches (Brier 0.047).
items.result: REFUTED - the pair is the last price held (updated in-play) and leaks the result; withdrawn from the method page.
items.note: The evaluation now publishes only the out-of-sample Bradley-Terry and Valve VRS rows; see irregularity IR-01.

items.claim: Every fixture the lobby lists is captured.
items.method: Parsed the fixture ids out of the lobby page's own transfer state and compared them with the lobby counters read the same minute.
items.result: 90 fixture ids captured; the lobby's own 'All tiers (89)' counter disagrees and is flagged (IR-02) rather than reconciled.
items.note: Counters: All 89 / B 25 / C 60 / S 4 and '68 matches this week'.

items.claim: Exchange quotes are only published inside the 0.20 spread limit and with volume or open interest.
items.method: Read KXCS2GAME-26OCT161400HAVUPHA (HAVU vs Phantom, stated start Oct 16 2:00 PM EDT = 18:00Z): HAVU yes 0.10/0.61, Phantom yes 0.42/0.82.
items.result: Refused as designed (spreads 0.51 / 0.40); the book stays on the flagged page as reference only.
items.note: Settlement sources published by Kalshi for this series: bo3.gg, hltv.org, egamersworld.com.

items.claim: A probability exists for every pickable fixture.
items.method: Compared data/coverage/ratings.json (349 rated teams) with the open fixtures whose teams are absent from the Valve snapshot.
items.result: REFUTED for those teams (WROTBERRY, RoundsGG, SUKEBAN, LFO 10): the rows stay blank and are published on the flagged page - never inferred.
items.note: The originated Bradley-Terry model needs at least 8 corpus matches per team, so it cannot cover them either yet (IR-05).

items.claim: The hourly job writes only session-owned paths.
items.method: Read .github/workflows/coverage-6ddde224.yml step by step: the commit step stages only `data/coverage/**` and `coverage/**`.
items.note: Collect step is tolerant by design (set +e) and always persists its log to data/coverage/collector_stdout.log.

items.claim: HotSpawn's crowd percentages are never a probability input.
items.method: Read the collector and builder line by line and ran the unit test that greps the collector for the crowd field and asserts no published probability can carry it.
items.note: The field is stored with a `_reference_only` suffix in the evidence files.

irregularities.finding: The first results crawl paginated wrong (the API ignored the plain `page` parameter): the committed corpus held 5,000 rows for 10 distinct matches, so the model evaluation carried by that snapshot is meaningless.
irregularities.evidence: distinct ids 10 / rows 5,000 (checked locally); bo3.gg `page[offset]` returns different matches per page
irregularities.affects: board model + evaluation of commit fdd22a0; the corpus is deleted, the collector now re-crawls such a snapshot, and the next run republishes the board

irregularities.finding: The lobby's own counters and the captured inventory disagree: 'All tiers (89)' vs 90 fixture ids rendered, and '68 matches this week' matches neither.
irregularities.affects: the listed_by_lobby figure; kept as captured and flagged, not silently reconciled

irregularities.finding: Elisa BreakOut start times drift up to ~2 h between the last committed data/live board and the current lobby listing.

irregularities.affects: start-time display and lock reminders; the board always keeps the source's own stated time and the next refresh is compared against it
